security_spec.violation_condition: When menvcfg.ADUE (or henvcfg.ADUE) is changed via CSR write, the XiangShan PTW/TLB may cache the A/D-bit-update-enable decision from the ADUE bit at the time of page walk inside TLB entries or PTW internal state. If SFENCE.VMA (or HFENCE.VVMA/HFENCE.GVMA) does not fully invalidate these cached entries, stale ADUE-dependent behavior persists: (a) ADUE 1→0 transition leaves TLB entries that still trigger hardware A/D writes to PTEs when Svade-mode should force page faults instead; (b) ADUE 0→1 transition leaves TLB entries that spuriously raise page faults when hardware should transparently set A/D bits.
security_spec.summary: menvcfg.ADUE change without full TLB flush: stale cached A/D hardware-update decisions in TLB/PTW can cause illegal PTE writes (ADUE 1→0) or spurious page faults (ADUE 0→1), violating the Svade/Svadu hardware-software contract

findings.finding: ADUE declared RO(reset=0) in base EnvCfg class. MEnvCfg, HEnvCfg, SEnvCfg all inherit without overriding to RW. Hardware A/D update is permanently disabled, matching the 'svade' ISA string advertisement. No writable path exists to toggle ADUE, so no stale-ADUE-in-TLB attack is possible.
MEnvCfg overrides STCE, PBMTE, DTE to RW but leaves ADUE as inherited RO=0. No mechanism to make menvcfg.ADUE writable. Correct for current svade-only implementation.
HEnvCfg mirrors MEnvCfg: overrides STCE, PBMTE, DTE to RW but leaves ADUE as inherited RO=0. Hypervisor-level envcfg ADUE is not writable, consistent with svade-only policy.
SEnvCfg is a bare extension of EnvCfg with no overrides—all fields including ADUE remain RO=0. Consistent with M/HS-level policy.
ISA string advertises 'svade' (not 'svadu'), correctly declaring A/D-bit faults are raised as page-fault exceptions rather than handled by hardware. Consistent with ADUE=RO=0.

A/D-bit updates (`ldUpdate`, `stUpdate`, `instrUpdate`) are flagged as conditions contributing to page-fault exceptions, not hardware PTE writes. This is correct Svade behavior: missing A/D bits → page fault → OS handles A/D software update.
findings.snippet:
val ldUpdate = !perm.a && isLd
val stUpdate = (!perm.a || !perm.d) && isSt
val instrUpdate = !perm.a && isInst

findings.finding: The TLB flush signal is composed as `sfence.valid || csr.satp.changed || csr.vsatp.changed || csr.hgatp.changed || csr.priv.virt_changed`. There is no `envcfg.changed` term. This is currently safe because ADUE is RO=0 (no change possible), and PBMTE/PMM changes propagate via RegNext in NewCSR.scala (lines 1480-1486), which does not require TLB invalidation per spec. However, if ADUE were ever made RW (to support Svadu), this flush composition would be architecturally insufficient—a stale-ADUE TLB entry could persist across an ADUE toggle without SFENCE.VMA.
findings.snippet: val flush_mmu = sfence.valid || csr.satp.changed || csr.vsatp.changed || csr.hgatp.changed || csr.priv.virt_changed

findings.finding: TlbCsrBundle carries `mPBMTE`, `hPBMTE`, and `pmm` (pointer masking) envcfg fields to the MMU subsystem, but has no `ADUE` field. Currently safe since ADUE is RO=0 and TLB always operates in Svade mode. If Svadu were added, this bundle would need an ADUE field so that the TLB/PTW permission check can conditionally skip raising page faults when hardware should transparently set A/D bits.

location.function_name: CSR→TLB envcfg forwarding (PBMTE via RegNext, no ADUE)

findings.finding: Only `PBMTE` and `PMM` envcfg fields are forwarded to the TLB via `RegNext` (one-cycle delay). ADUE is neither forwarded nor has a `changed` detection signal. The PR context states that 'ADUE updates be synchronized in a fashion analogous to PBMTE.' However, PBMTE's RegNext-only synchronization is correct because PBMTE changes don't invalidate cached translations—they only affect interpretation of new PTE PBMT bits. ADUE is fundamentally different: toggling ADUE changes whether cached A/D=0 TLB entries should fault (Svade) or be silently updated (Svadu). RegNext-only would NOT suffice; a proper TLB invalidate or at minimum an `adue.changed` signal feeding the flush composition is architecturally required.

Same pattern as TLB flush: L2TLB flush lacks `envcfg.changed`. The flush composition across ALL MMU components (L2TLB, L2TLBMissQueue, L2TlbPrefetch, PageTableWalker, PageTableCache, BitmapCheck, Repeater) is identically `sfence || satp.changed || vsatp.changed || hgatp.changed || virt_changed` with no envcfg change term. If ADUE were made RW, all these locations would need updating.
findings.snippet: val flush = sfence_dup(0).valid || satp.changed || vsatp.changed || hgatp.changed || priv.virt_changed

findings.finding: PTW flush composition mirrors TLB/L2TLB: no envcfg.changed term. Additionally, PTW does not select ADUE from CSR bundle to gate hardware A/D-bit writes (no such logic exists). If ADUE were made RW and hardware A/D updates implemented in the PTW FSM, the PTW would need both the ADUE signal and proper flush-on-change behavior.
findings.snippet: val flush = io.sfence.valid || io.csr.satp.changed || io.csr.vsatp.changed || io.csr.hgatp.changed || io.csr.priv.virt_changed
